description: In November 2024 artist Helena Roden was commissioned to work with Camden’s Bangladeshi community to collaborate on the design of a new public artwork which celebrates the spirit of the community. This artwork commission will deliver on an important action point in Camden’s Strategy for Diversity in the Public Realm and the We Make Camden vision. The Bangladeshi community selected for this work as they are Camden’s largest minority ethnic group and are often overlooked and underrepresented in Camden’s public realm. Argyle Square was selected as the location for the sculpture after discussion with ward councillors, community and public consultation. The sculptural work was developed with Bangladeshi communities in surrounding neighbourhoods. The design was informed by creative workshops and storytelling with these communities. The sculpture design is a structure of abstracted shapes referencing elements of Bangladeshi culture including sari patterns, Bangla language, the sun and the Shaheed Minar (the monument to Bangladesh’s Language Movement). The pierced design of the central red disc includes motifs from South Asian textiles, embroidery and henna hand painting which came through community workshops. The openwork design will also use the sun to cast interesting shadow patterns onto the grass of the garden. The white uprights supporting the disc reference the uprights of the Shaheed Minar, an important cultural site for people with Bangladeshi heritage. Two letters on the sculpture form the word মা which are the Bangla letters that spell MA (mother) as proposed by the KCNBA Youth Club, based nearby in Argyle Street. The local mosque is sited on the corner of Argyle square. The proposed sculpture is abstract in design and can be enjoyed by all communities using Argyle Square. It will become an important site for Camden’s Bangladeshi community, where families can come together for reflection and sharing stories and culture, enjoying the gardens which are currently under-used by the community. The overall height of the sculpture is 3m, with the central disc diameter of 1.1m. The sculpture will be made from mild steel, galvanised against rust, with an acid-etched primer and resin-paint top coat. Foundations will be a sunken concrete slab to which the elements are bolted. the space back-filled by soil and planted over. The sculpture will be constructed to a tried and tested high specification for minimal future maintenance. It is proposed that the sculpture will be sited in a garden bed in the central part of the square. This garden bed will be planted with plants relevant to the community, in partnership with the Bangladeshi community (Chadswell Healthy Living centre gardening club) and Camden’s Green Spaces team.
